issues.legal_issue: A purchaser at an execution sale under a decree against a father may acquire his sons’ interests in joint family property for a non-immoral debt even when the father was not the family manager and the sons were not parties to the suit or execution proceedings.
material_facts: The debtor was a father in an undivided Hindu family that included his sons and other coparceners; he was not the family manager.
The father had borrowed money, and the debt was not shown to be immoral or irreligious.
A decree was obtained against the father alone, and the execution sale was found to include the interests of the father’s sons.
The sons had an opportunity in the partition suit to assert that the debt was not binding on them, but did not establish that claim.
issues.conclusion: The purchaser acquired the sons’ interests included in the execution sale, and the purchaser was entitled to the claimed one-fourth share.
issues.legal_principle: Under Mitakshara Hindu law, sons’ interests in coparcenary property are liable for their father’s debts that are not tainted with immorality or irreligion. That liability is not limited by the father’s power of voluntary disposition, nor does it depend on his being the karta or on the family consisting only of the father and sons. Under the rule in Nanomi Babuasin v. Modun Mohun, a creditor may have the sons’ interests sold without joining them, subject to their right to establish that the debt is not binding on them. The Court relied also on Pannalal v. Mst. Naraini and approved Lalta Prashad v. Gazadhar, Chhotey Lal v. Ganpat, and Virayya v. Parthasarathi.

rule.if: execution_sale_case and father_contracted_debt and debt_not_immoral_or_irreligious and sale_included_sons_interests

predicates.execution_sale_case: A creditor obtained a decree against a member of an undivided Hindu family and sought to enforce it by selling an interest in joint family property.
predicates.father_contracted_debt: The debtor was the father of sons whose interests in the joint family property were at issue, and he contracted the debt.
predicates.debt_not_immoral_or_irreligious: The debt was not shown to have been tainted with immorality or irreligion.
predicates.sale_included_sons_interests: The execution sale was intended to include, and did include, the sons’ interests in the joint family property.

issues.definition: When a decree against a father in an undivided Hindu family is enforced by a sale that includes his sons’ interests, the purchaser acquires those interests if the father contracted a debt not shown to be immoral or irreligious.

issues.legal_issue: A purchaser of an undivided interest in joint family property at an execution sale cannot recover a share of the family’s income or obtain possession before a partition makes a specific allotment to the purchaser.
material_facts: The purchaser acquired an undivided interest in joint family property at an execution sale.
The purchaser sued the other family members for a share of the income or profits from the properties from the date of purchase.
No specific portion of the property had been allotted to the purchaser by partition.
issues.conclusion: The purchaser could not recover a share of the income or profits from the date of purchase; the purchaser had to pursue partition, and the right to possession would begin when a specific allotment was made.
issues.legal_principle: An execution purchaser of an undivided coparcenary interest acquires no title to a defined portion of the property and is not entitled to joint possession from the date of purchase. The purchaser must work out the acquired rights through a partition suit, with possession beginning when a specific allotment is made.

predicates.execution_purchase_case: A purchaser acquired an interest in joint family property through an execution sale.
predicates.purchased_interest_undivided: The interest acquired was undivided and did not identify a specific portion of the property.
predicates.no_specific_allotment: A partition had not made a specific allotment of property to the purchaser.

issues.definition: A purchaser of an undivided interest cannot claim family income or possession before a partition makes a specific allotment to the purchaser.
